assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (magic-wavelength trapping, proposed by Katori, realized to 1e-18 uncertainty and below) opened a new regime of precision measurement, with consequences for redefining the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is original, clean and experimentally decisive, and the impact on metrology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names form a natural pair: Katori invented the lattice-clock concept and magic wavelength, Jun Ye drove the best-performing systems and many-body/spin-exchange extensions. The attribution is compact, and I regard it as fair, although others in the clock community (for example ion-clock and Sr-clock groups) contributed to the surrounding ecosystem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent laboratories worldwide over two decades, with international comparisons and a pending redefinition roadmap for the second. The interpretation is stable; recognition is timely and arguably overdue, since the field is mature while still advancing.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of optical frequency combs and ion-trap clocks may be raised.
Whether the redefinition of the SI second, which has not yet occurred, is needed before recognition.
I rely on my own background knowledge of credit and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of twistronics and moire quantum matter. This is highly original, conceptually clean, and has had an enormous impact across condensed matter, with a decisive theory-experiment pairing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery. A fair trio exists, but the two theorists share one contribution and Bistritzer's role relative to MacDonald's is a judgment call; the experimental credit also involves the Cao and Fatemi coworkers and competing groups (for example Dean, Young, Yazdani and others on related moire systems), so the allocation is not wholly settled.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the results and extended them to other moire systems (fractional Chern insulators, TMD moire). The interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still debated, so the maturity of the broader programme is partial, but the core discovery is solidly confirmed.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is unresolved.
Allocation among theory credits (Bistritzer, MacDonald, others such as Santos and Lopes dos Santos) and experimental credits.
Prize timing may be considered early relative to the technological outcome.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube discovery of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux (2013), followed by the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, established neutrino astronomy as a new window on the extreme universe. It combines a heroic instrumentation effort (a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice) with a clear discovery. As an astroparticle experimentalist I regard the detector concept and its execution as outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the principal investigator and concept driver; Karle and Spiering are long-standing key figures in construction and analysis. A kilometre-scale collaboration of about 300 members makes any three-person selection incomplete, and the contributions of AMANDA/Baikal and Kamiokande-type predecessors (some already recognized in 2002) complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed in multiple channels and by KM3NeT/Baikal-GVD early results. Source identification is only partly established (a few sources at 3-4 sigma), so some of the interpretation is still developing, but the discovery of the flux itself is robust.
uncertainties: Whether the source identifications are mature enough, and whether the discovery should be emphasized over the detector.
Credit boundaries within a large collaboration and the relationship to earlier ice-Cherenkov pioneers.
My field proximity may bias me toward the instrumentation; I have tried to apply the same criteria as for other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 confirmed the mechanism recognized by the 2013 prize and is a monumental achievement in detector science, trigger design and large-scale analysis. Its importance is beyond question; the issue is that the theory was already honoured, so the remaining question is whether the experimental discovery merits its own recognition.
assessment.attribution: The proposals and construction leadership of ATLAS and CMS are credited to Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee, with Gianotti as the ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery and Evans as LHC project leader. The three-laureate limit forces difficult choices: accelerator, two detectors and thousands of collaborators. I choose the experiment founders, but this allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: both experiments independently observed the particle, and coupling measurements now agree with the Standard Model within about 10 percent. Recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Precedent of the 2013 prize may reduce appetite for a second Higgs prize.
The choice among Gianotti, Evans, Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee is unresolved.
Whether collaboration-scale discoveries are a good fit to the prize statutes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The demonstration of optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond at room temperature led to a platform for nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and quantum registers. It is original and technically elegant, with a wide range of applications from biology to condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the single-NV optical detection and coherent control experiments; Lukin and collaborators (together with Walsworth and others) developed the sensing proposals and quantum-register work. The credit is shared across several groups, and the trio is plausible but not unique (Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby and others contributed to spin control and sensing).
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced, commercialized, and a mainstay of quantum sensing. Some applications, such as in-vivo and NMR-scale sensing, are still maturing, but the underlying discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Boundary between the original single-defect discovery and the sensing applications.
Large and potentially competing credit among Awschalom, Hanson, Walsworth, Yacoby and others.
Overlap with quantum-information recognition may complicate packaging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The WMAP (and Planck) precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies established the Lambda-CDM parameters to percent level and underpins modern cosmology. The importance and lasting impact are very high, though COBE's 2006 prize already recognised the discovery of anisotropies and the blackbody spectrum.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the WMAP mission, Page contributed critically to the instrument and calibration, and Spergel to the cosmological analysis. Puget and the Planck/HFI team form an alternative allocation, and large-mission credit is diffuse. The listed trio is reasonable, but the choice among WMAP and Planck leaders is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, with several independent datasets (WMAP, Planck, ACT, SPT) in agreement; tensions such as the Hubble tension are about the model, not the measurements.
uncertainties: Whether the 2006 and 2019 prizes make another cosmology prize less likely.
Allocation between WMAP and Planck leaders and the instrument builders.
Recognition might focus on parameters rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are a spectacular, publicly legible test of strong-field gravity and a triumph of very-long-baseline interferometry, calibration and imaging. The scientific content is rich, though the images are mainly confirmatory of general relativity rather than revealing new physics.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT, Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, and Moran pioneered the mm-VLBI technique. A collaboration of about 300 and the contributions of many VLBI pioneers make any trio contentious; this is the most difficult attribution of those I rank.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: M87* was imaged in 2019 and Sgr A* in 2022, with multi-epoch and polarization follow-up. Independent confirmation by other collaborations is limited, and interpretation of the accretion flow remains model dependent.
uncertainties: Credit within a large collaboration and among VLBI pioneers.
The images are consistent with GR; the novelty of the physics is debated.
Limited independent confirmation, since only one collaboration can currently produce such images.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon pixel and microstrip tracking detectors enabled vertexing and tracking in high-rate collider experiments, and the Higgs, heavy-flavour and many other discoveries rely on them. The same technology went to medical and space applications. As an instrumentalist I consider this deeply important, though it is a technology prize case rather than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Heijne and colleagues (hybrid pixel detectors at CERN), Parker (silicon microstrip detectors) and Snoeys (monolithic and readout electronics) are plausible, but credit across the community (Rossi, Kemmer, Hallewell, Campbell and others) is distributed, so the three-person choice is quite uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: the devices are used in all major collider experiments and in X-ray imaging. Recognition of detector inventions has occurred in the past (Charpak 1992), but is rare, and the history of the credit is complicated.
uncertainties: Genuine conflict between a technology-and-instrument prize and the preference for discovery.
Highly distributed credit in the detector community.
My own detector background could incline me favourably; the case is a long shot.
